Leontief’s L-shaped contours draw properly, including vertical arm, mrs() gives textbook answer: Inf ray, 0 , NA kink.  Anything isn’t one still works: pass function x y contours found bisection, optimum line search along budget line — every closed form tested generic path. Ask optimum question many times get derived curves: geom_demand() draws price quantity way textbooks ; geom_budget() takes list budgets family lines behind path one layer.  diagram every intermediate course draws: price change , split part relative prices part poorer. Hicks compensation holds utility fixed; Slutsky holds purchasing power fixed. rest expenditure(), expenditure function, dedicated method every constructor doubles total-cost function producer side.  producer’s side mathematics different names — production function utility function inputs, isocost line budget line, expenditure function total-cost function — comes free:  Put demand curve front costs market: Every structure returns market_outcome — price, quantities, profit, consumer producer surplus, deadweight loss P = MC benchmark, Lerner index — plot_market() draws welfare areas shaded. Costs can also come straight production function via production_cost(), decreasing function(q) works demand.  monopolist one price: third_degree() carries uniform-price benchmark (via aggregate_demand(), horizontal sum), gain segmenting explicit inverse-elasticity rule holds segment segment. two_part_tariff() weighs serving everyone — fee pinned lightest user, unit price marginal cost — excluding light users taking heavy users’ whole surplus.

title: Augmented Dickey-Fuller test for a unit root — adf_test
text: Estimates \(\Delta y_t = \alpha + \beta t + \gamma y_{t-1} + \sum_{=1}^{p} \phi_i \Delta y_{t-} + \varepsilon_t\) tests \(\gamma = 0\) (unit root) \(\gamma < 0\) (stationarity) t statistic \(\gamma\). null statistic t distribution; critical values come MacKinnon's (2010) response surfaces, adjust sample size.

title: Augmented Dickey-Fuller test for a unit root — adf_test
code: adf_test(x, lags = NULL, type = c("drift", "trend", "none"), max_lags = NULL)

title: Augmented Dickey-Fuller test for a unit root — adf_test
text: x numeric vector, single-series data frame value column. lags Number lagged differences p. NULL lag length chosen AIC 0:max_lags. type Deterministic terms: "drift", "trend" "none". max_lags Upper bound AIC search. Defaults Schwert's \(\lfloor 12 (T/100)^{1/4} \rfloor\).

title: Augmented Dickey-Fuller test for a unit root — adf_test
text: object class adf_test: list statistic, critical (named vector 1, 5 10 percent), reject (logical, per level), lags, type, nobs fitted regression. p-value reported; compare statistic critical values, printer .

title: Augmented Dickey-Fuller test for a unit root — adf_test
text: Choose type series looks like alternative: "drift" (default) series fluctuates around non-zero level, "trend" one grows, "none" series known centred zero. Including deterministic terms data need costs power; leaving terms need makes test invalid.

title: Augmented Dickey-Fuller test for a unit root — adf_test
text: MacKinnon, J. G. (2010). Critical values cointegration tests. Queen's Economics Department Working Paper 1227. Said, S. E. Dickey, D. . (1984). Testing unit roots autoregressive-moving average models unknown order. Biometrika 71(3).

title: Augmented Dickey-Fuller test for a unit root — adf_test
code: set.seed(1) rw <- cumsum(rnorm(200))         # a random walk: do not reject adf_test(rw) #> <Augmented Dickey-Fuller test: constant, 0 lagged differences, 199 observations> #>   statistic -2.132 #>     1% critical value -3.464  cannot reject #>     5% critical value -2.876  cannot reject #>    10% critical value -2.574  cannot reject  ar <- as.numeric(stats::arima.sim(list(ar = 0.5), 200))   # stationary: reject adf_test(ar) #> <Augmented Dickey-Fuller test: constant, 0 lagged differences, 199 observations> #>   statistic -8.543 #>     1% critical value -3.464  reject unit root #>     5% critical value -2.876  reject unit root #>    10% critical value -2.574  reject unit root
